chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: Hawkins band at Billy Berg's and the film Crimson Canary
summary: The inventive band with Howard McGhee played Billy Berg's and appeared in a film, The Crimson Canary, where music was pre-recorded.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But the main thing I wanted to speak about about this group was that it was a very musical group and it was very inventive. Everybody in the band was a writer, you know. Denzil Best wrote music.
And we played some of his music. McGhee And then there was Howard McGee, a very, very fine trumpet player.

Unfortunately he had some bad luck, physical handicaps, and later on he -- well, the band didn't stay together too long either. We came to Hollywood and we played Billy Berg's for a short period, and then we made this picture that featured our band in a moving picture that was made with Noah Beery Jr., and some other people. I think the name of the picture was the "Crimson Canary Murder Case".
And we had a scene in there playing in a jazz club.
Oh. Have you ever seen it since?
Yes, I saw it in New York when it first came out, you know. It wasn't a very good picture, but it was exciting to see myself bow in the picture.
Yes. It must have been a very good musical sequence too, wasn't it.

Some of the music was good, but it wasn't the best because unfortunately because of the technical-ities in those days of the -- the music was recorded at one time, and you had to pretend you were playing, and some of the

things that weren't compatible to the feeling of jazz, some of the recordings didn't come off too good. But there were also some very good ones. Some of the ones that I'm very proud to have been on, some of my favorite recordings that I've made were made on those Capitol Albums that were made during that time. It was called "Hollywood Stampede".
